answer: Jade Embarkation Ledger. Each identity receives a unique departure shard at first action; the shard must be presented, along with a signed voyage log, before any second action is accepted. Duplicate shards are detected because the ledger records every embarkation and rejects any shard not matching its original bearer. An attacker cloning an identity must forge a relic of the original shard, which costs a full recomputation of the chain's state proof per duplicate.
